title: Latency-aware dedicated throughput SLA, error budget tiers, and contractual remediation language
creator: Asha Patel
description: Define a latency-aware throughput SLA that ties guaranteed throughput to both per-minute throughput targets and latency SLOs (P50/P95/P99). Produce clear error-budget tiers, a deterministic crediting algorithm, and contract-ready remediation language. Ensure autoscaling and fleet controls integrate with the SLA so that remediation steps (credits, capacity add, and graceful degradation) are predictable and auditable.
background: Customers on Dedicated pools have requested guarantees that reflect both throughput and tail latency. Current documents focus on throughput quantiles alone and create mismatch when large models or noisy workloads cause latency spikes even while throughput targets are near nominal. Sales/legal need a single contract annex with measurable definitions for automated error budgeting, billing credits, and operational backstops that map to runbook actions (burst buys, prioritized-service lanes, and temporary capacity shifts).
success_metrics: 1) SLA measurement and crediting implemented in billing pipeline; 2) 95% of escalations resolved via documented backstops within defined remediation windows; 3) Reduced customer-reported degraded-throughput incidents by 30% in next quarter.
sla_definition: Measurement window: rolling 30-day window with daily buckets for visibility. Primary metric: Guaranteed throughput (tokens/sec or requests/sec) at a target latency cap. Latency caps: P50 <= 80ms, P95 <= 250ms, P99 <= 800ms (per-customer, per-AZ, measured at ingress). Throughput guarantee expressed as the 50th percentile of per-minute throughput over the 30-day window (configurable in contract). Non-overlapping maintenance windows excluded if pre-notified. Synthetic probe traffic and tenant instrumentation will be used to disambiguate noisy customer traffic from platform degradation.
error_budget_policy: Error budgets computed separately for throughput and latency. Each customer gets a monthly error budget expressed in 'degradation points' (DP). DP accrues when either throughput falls below guaranteed throughput for >1 minute or when P99 latency exceeds the latency cap for >1 minute. Severity weights: throughput shortfall weight = 1 DP per minute of 10% deficit; latency P99 breach weight = 2 DP per minute. Budgets tiered: Standard (30 DP/month), Elevated (15 DP/month), Enterprise (60 DP/month) — configurable by contract. Exhaustion triggers remediation buckets (see crediting and backstops).
crediting_algorithm: When error budget is spent beyond the allowance, billing credits are computed as a function of the fraction of hours impacted and tier. Example formula: credit = min(0.5 * committed_monthly_fee * (minutes_impacted / total_billable_minutes), cap) where cap = 25% of monthly committed fee for a single incident. For repeat or prolonged incidents (>=12 hours cumulative in 30-day window) escalation to pro-rata refunds and engineering priority is triggered. Credits are computed weekly and available on the next invoice. All calculations logged and exposed via the customer Console transparency panel.
autoscaling_interaction: Autoscaling policies are first-class inputs to the SLA. By default, Dedicated pools have an autoscale guard that will attempt to add capacity automatically up to the customer's configured burst cap. If latency breaches are detected despite autoscale attempts (no available capacity in-region), the system will: 1) open a degraded-priority lane to shed best-effort background workloads, 2) attempt cross-AZ overflow routing if permitted, 3) notify customer with recommended temporary burst purchase. Contracts can opt-in to 'aggressive autoscale' (higher burst cap, faster spin-up) for higher fee. Autoscale increases do not reset error budget retroactively; they mitigate future minutes.
fleet_control_guards: Implement fleet-level safeguards to avoid noisy neighbor amplification: 1) Per-tenant per-instance CPU/GPU fairshare with backpressure; 2) Global admission control that throttles new low-priority sessions when a customer's P99 breaches by >2x; 3) Safe-rollover policy for model rollouts—no single AZ can consume >40% of free capacity for the pool during rollouts. All control actions are recorded with causal metadata to support audit and contract disputes.
contract_clause_examples: Service Guarantee. Redwood guarantees a committed throughput capacity as specified in Attachment A and will use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain latency caps (P50/P95/P99) as measured at the customer edge. Measurement uses a rolling 30-day window with daily observability buckets.

Error Budget & Credits. Customer is allocated an Error Budget expressed as Degradation Points. When the Error Budget is exhausted due to platform degradation, Redwood will apply credits to the next invoice according to the crediting algorithm in Section X. Credits are the exclusive monetary remedy for SLA breaches except in cases of willful misconduct.

Autoscale & Burst. Redwood will attempt automated capacity remediation based on the customer's configured autoscale profile. If autoscale is unavailable due to regional capacity constraints, Redwood will notify the customer and provide recommended temporary capacity options. If agreed-upon burst purchases are used, charges will appear as a line-item and do not negate credit eligibility for the original incident window.

Operational Backstops. For incidents exceeding 6 cumulative hours of sustained degradation in a 30-day window, Redwood will: (a) escalate to Product & Engineering priority, (b) offer temporary capacity migration where feasible, and (c) provide an incident report with root cause analysis and remediation plan within 10 business days.
implementation_notes: Billing: extend billing pipeline to accept DP events and compute credits weekly (owner: billing eng).
Telemetry: add per-tenant P99 measurement at ingress and synthetic probes; store 1-min resolution metrics for 90 days (owner: obs team).
Policy: add contract template annex and checkbox for aggressive autoscale/burst opt-in (owner: legal & sales).
Runbook: update Dedicated on-call runbook with escalation triggers for DP thresholds (owner: SRE).
